title: The eight curve assertions and restriction to a dense open
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of characteristic exponent $p$, let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ with $\dim X\le1$, and let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ which is constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion], so that $(X,F)$ is a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. Let $j:X'\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of a dense open subscheme, $j^{-1}F$ the restriction of $F$ to $X'$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $j_!j^{-1}F$ its extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], again a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$. Let $\mathcal C(X,-)$ be the eight assertions of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], each read as an implication that holds when its hypotheses fail (Stacks, Situation 0A52: 'those statements that apply'). Then:
1. If $\mathcal C(X,j_!j^{-1}F)$ holds, then $\mathcal C(X,F)$ holds.
2. If $\mathcal C(X,F)$ holds and $F$ is $p$-primary or prime to $p$ [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion] (in characteristic $0$ this is no condition; it holds whenever $F$ is killed by a prime number), then $\mathcal C(X,j_!j^{-1}F)$ holds.
In particular, for $F$ killed by a prime number, $\mathcal C(X,F)$ holds if and only if $\mathcal C(X,j_!j^{-1}F)$ holds.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Section 03SB (section-vanishing-torsion), Lemma 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), with Situation 0A52; the proof uses the sequence of Lemma 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), Proposition 03QP and the Leray spectral sequence for the closed immersion of the finite set Z = X \ X' of k-points

proof.text: Conventions. Write $F'=j_!j^{-1}F$. As in Stacks, Situation 0A52 ('we will say that statements (1)-(8) hold if those statements that apply to the given situation are true'), $\mathcal C(X,G)$ for a curve coefficient pair $(X,G)$ is the conjunction of the eight implications $\mathcal C_1,\dots,\mathcal C_8$ [def-weil-pbc-C1]-[def-weil-pbc-C8] of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]; Stacks' items (1) item-vanishing, (2) item-vanishing-affine, (3) item-vanishing-p-p, (4) item-finite-prime-to-p, (5) item-finite-proper, (6) item-base-change-prime-to-p, (7) item-base-change-proper, (8) item-surjective are $\mathcal C_1,\dots,\mathcal C_8$ in this order, and Lemma 0GJA covers all eight. For the zero sheaf every conclusion holds trivially (all cohomology groups and pullback maps are those of $0$). By [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion], when $\operatorname{char}k=0$ every torsion sheaf is prime to the characteristic and $(\mathcal C_3)$ is vacuous; so the case analyses below on '$p$-primary / prime to $p$' only concern $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$.

source.place: Situation 0A52 (situation-what-to-prove) and the list (1)-(8) after it

proof.text: The closed complement (Stacks 0GJA, proof, first sentence: 'Since $X'$ is dense, we see that $Z=X\setminus X'$ has dimension $0$ and hence is a finite set of $k$-rational points'). $X$ is of finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian, with finitely many irreducible components $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generic points $\eta_a$. The open set $X_a\setminus\bigcup_{b\ne a}X_b$ is nonempty and contains $\eta_a$; the dense open $X'$ meets it in a point $y$ with $y\in\overline{\{\eta_a\}}$, so $\eta_a\in X'$ as $X'$ is open. Hence $Z=X\setminus X'$ contains no $\eta_a$: for $z\in Z$ lying in $X_a$, $\overline{\{z\}}$ is a proper irreducible closed subset of $X_a$, which has dimension $\le1$, so $\overline{\{z\}}=\{z\}$. Thus $Z$, closed in the Noetherian $X$, has finitely many irreducible components, each a closed point: $Z=\{z_1,\dots,z_n\}$ is finite and discrete. Give $Z$ its reduced induced structure, with closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; $Z$ is a separated $k$-scheme of finite type of dimension $\le0$ (possibly empty), each $z_m$ has residue field finite over $k$, hence equal to $k$ (Nullstellensatz), so $z_m:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ is a geometric point $\bar z_m$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and $i$ is finite (a closed immersion). For every open $U\subseteq X$ the same holds for $Z_U=Z\cap U=U\times_XZ$, an open subscheme of $Z$, with closed immersion $i_U:Z_U\hookrightarrow U$; and $X'\cap U$ is dense in $U$ (Stacks remark (d)).

source.place: Lemma 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof, first sentence, and remark (d)

proof.text: The exact sequence and stalks (Stacks 0GJA, proof: 'Consider the short exact sequence of Lemma 095L'). Put $E=i^{-1}F$ on $Z_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $G=i_*E$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Since $X'=X\setminus i(Z)$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] gives the exact sequence $0\to F'\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}F\xrightarrow{\eta}G\to0$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$. Geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] are filtered colimits, hence exact, so for every geometric point $\bar x$ the stalk $F'_{\bar x}$ is a subgroup of $F_{\bar x}$ and $G_{\bar x}$ a quotient of it. Consequently: $F'$ and $G$ are torsion (a local section of the subsheaf $F'$ is one of $F$; a local section of $G$ lifts locally to $F$), so $(X,F')$, $(X,G)$ are curve coefficient pairs [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]; if $F$ is $p$-primary (resp. prime to $p$) [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion], so are $F'$ and $G$ (their stalk elements are elements, resp. images of elements, of stalks of $F$). Moreover, if $F$ is prime to $p$ and $F'$ is $p$-primary, or $F$ is $p$-primary and $F'$ is prime to $p$, then every element of every $F'_{\bar x}$ has order both a power of $p$ and prime to $p$, so all stalks of $F'$ vanish and $F'=0$ by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] applied to $0\to F'$.

source.place: Lemma 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof, the sequence of Lemma 095L and remark (a)

proof.text: Cohomology of $G$ (Stacks 0GJA, proof: '$H^q(X,i_*i^{-1}F)=H^q(Z,i^*F)$ ... by Proposition 03QP and the Leray spectral sequence; since $Z$ is a disjoint union of spectra of algebraically closed fields, $H^q(Z,i^*F)=0$ for $q>0$ and $H^0=\bigoplus F_{x_i}$, which is finite as $F$ is constructible'). Since $i$ is finite, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] gives $Ri_*E\cong i_*E=G$ in $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, and part 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit] (for $u=i$, $L=E$) gives $\RGamma(X_{\Et},Ri_*E)\cong\RGamma(Z_{\Et},E)$; taking $\mathcal H^q$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $H^q(X,G)\cong H^q(Z,E)$ for all $q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology] for the zero-dimensional $Z$ (step 2): $H^q(Z,E)=0$ for $q>0$ and $H^0(Z,E)=\prod_{m}E_{\bar z_m}$, a finite product. Each $E_{\bar z_m}$ is finite: the geometric fibre of the closed immersion $i$ over $\bar z_m$ is the single geometric point $\bar z_m$ of $Z$, so [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] gives $E_{\bar z_m}\cong(i_*E)_{\bar z_m}=G_{\bar z_m}$, a quotient of $F_{\bar z_m}$ (step 3); and $F_{\bar z_m}$ is finite because $F$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]: $z_m$ lies in a stratum $S$ of the partition, and the stalk of $F$ at the geometric point $\bar z_m$ of $S$ is the stalk there of the restriction $F|_S$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] (the inverse image along an immersion does not change stalks, Stacks 03Q1), which is locally constant with finite stalks. Hence $H^q(X,G)=0$ for $q\ge1$ and $H^0(X,G)$ is finite.

source.place: Lemma 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof, second and third sentences; Proposition 03QP; Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 0733

proof.text: Restriction of $G$ to an open (needed for $(\mathcal C_8)$; Stacks remark (d)). Let $a:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion, $Z_U=U\times_XZ$ with $i_U:Z_U\hookrightarrow U$ and open immersion $a_Z:Z_U\hookrightarrow Z$ (step 2). For an open immersion the inverse image is restriction: $(a^{-1}H)(V\to U)=H(V\to U\to X)$ for $V\in U_{\Et}$, naturally in $V$ and the sheaf $H$ (the identification in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], Stacks 03S3 and the discussion after it). Hence, using $(i_*E)(W)=E(W\times_XZ)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and $V\times_XZ=V\times_U(U\times_XZ)=V\times_UZ_U$, an etale $Z_U$-scheme: $(a^{-1}G)(V)=E(V\times_XZ)=(a_Z^{-1}E)(V\times_UZ_U)=(i_{U*}a_Z^{-1}E)(V)$, naturally in $V$; so $a^{-1}G\cong i_{U*}(a_Z^{-1}E)$. As in step 4 (with $U$, $Z_U$, $i_U$ for $X$, $Z$, $i$; $Z_U$ is zero-dimensional, separated and of finite type over $k$, $i_U$ finite), $H^q(U,a^{-1}G)\cong H^q(Z_U,a_Z^{-1}E)=0$ for $q\ge1$.

source.place: Lemma 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof, remark (d); Definition 03S3 and the discussion after it

proof.text: The assertions for $G$ (Stacks 0GJA, proof, remark (c): '$H^0(Z,i^{-1}F)=H^0(Z_{k'},i^{-1}F|_{Z_{k'}})$'; written via Lemma 0A5D). $(Z,E)$ is a curve coefficient pair: $E=i^{-1}F$ is torsion, as the inverse image of a torsion sheaf (it is the sheafification of a presheaf whose values are colimits of groups of sections of $F$, [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]). $\mathcal C(Z,E)$ holds: by step 4 the groups $H^q(Z,E)$ vanish for $q\ge1$ and $H^0(Z,E)$ is finite, which gives the conclusions of $(\mathcal C_1)$-$(\mathcal C_5)$ whatever the hypotheses; every open $Z''\subseteq Z$ is again zero-dimensional, so $H^2(Z'',E|_{Z''})=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology] and $(\mathcal C_8)$ holds; $(\mathcal C_6)$ and $(\mathcal C_7)$ hold by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-field-extension] ($\rho^q_{k'/k}(Z,E)$ is an isomorphism for every $q$ and every algebraically closed $k'/k$). Since $i:Z\to X$ is a finite morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes of dimension $\le1$, [lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-finite-pushforward] (Stacks 0A5D) gives $\mathcal C(X,G)=\mathcal C(X,i_*E)$. In particular $\rho^q_{k'/k}(X,G)$ is an isomorphism for all $q$ when $X$ is proper ($\mathcal C_7$), or when $G$ is prime to $p$ ($\mathcal C_6$).

Long exact sequences and ladders (Stacks 0GJA, proof: 'The long exact cohomology sequence gives an exact sequence $0\to H^0(X,j_!j^{-1}F)\to H^0(X,F)\to H^0(Z,i^{-1}F)\to H^1(X,j_!j^{-1}F)\to H^1(X,F)\to0$ and isomorphisms $H^q(X,j_!j^{-1}F)\to H^q(X,F)$ for $q>1$'). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] to the sequence of step 3, once with $u=\pi_{k'}:X_{k'}\to X$ for an algebraically closed $k'/k$ (the pullback maps $u^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] are then the maps $\rho^q_{k'/k}$ of [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback]) and once with $u=a:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion: the pulled-back sequences $0\to u^{-1}F'\to u^{-1}F\to u^{-1}G\to0$ are exact, and the long exact cohomology sequences on $X$ and on $X_{k'}$ (resp. $U$) are connected by a morphism of long exact sequences given by $\rho$ (resp. $a^*$). With step 4 ($H^q(X,G)=0$ for $q\ge1$) the sequence on $X$ yields: (i) $H^q(X,F')\to H^q(X,F)$ is an isomorphism for $q\ge2$; (ii) $0\to H^0(X,F')\to H^0(X,F)\to H^0(X,G)\to H^1(X,F')\to H^1(X,F)\to0$ is exact. With step 5 ($H^1(U,a^{-1}G)=0$) the sequence on $U$ yields: (iii) $H^2(U,a^{-1}F')\to H^2(U,a^{-1}F)$ is injective.

source.place: Lemma 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof, the long exact cohomology sequence

proof.text: Part 1: $\mathcal C(X,F')\Rightarrow\mathcal C(X,F)$ (Stacks writes 'at this point it is easy to deduce each of (1)-(8) holds for $F$ if and only if it holds for $j_!j^{-1}F$'; this direction is the dévissage of Lemma 0A5C, outer terms to middle). The sequence $0\to F'\to F\to G\to0$ of step 3 is a short exact sequence of torsion sheaves on $X_{\Et}$; $\mathcal C(X,F')$ holds by hypothesis and $\mathcal C(X,G)$ by step 6. Hence [lemma-weil-pbc-eight-curve-devissage] (Stacks 0A5C) gives $\mathcal C(X,F)$.

Part 2, assertions $(\mathcal C_1)$, $(\mathcal C_2)$, $(\mathcal C_3)$. The converse cannot use Lemma 0A5C (that lemma passes from the outer terms to the middle, and here $F'$ is the sub); Stacks deduces it from the cohomology sequence, assertion by assertion, which is done here and in the next three steps. Assume $\mathcal C(X,F)$ and that $F$ is $p$-primary or prime to $p$. $(\mathcal C_1)$: for $q>2$, $H^q(X,F')\cong H^q(X,F)=0$ by step 7(i) and $\mathcal C_1(X,F)$ [def-weil-pbc-C1]. $(\mathcal C_2)$: if $X$ is affine, for $q>1$, $H^q(X,F')\cong H^q(X,F)=0$ by 7(i) and $\mathcal C_2(X,F)$ [def-weil-pbc-C2]. $(\mathcal C_3)$ [def-weil-pbc-C3]: let $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $F'$ be $p$-primary. If $F$ is $p$-primary, $H^q(X,F')\cong H^q(X,F)=0$ for $q>1$ by 7(i) and $\mathcal C_3(X,F)$; if $F$ is prime to $p$, then $F'=0$ by step 3 and the conclusion is trivial. (The hypothesis on $F$ is what makes this possible: without it, $F$ could be $j_!j^{-1}$ of a $p$-primary sheaf plus a sheaf supported on $Z$ that is not $p$-primary, and then $\mathcal C(X,F)$ says nothing about $H^q(X,F')$ unless $X$ is affine; this is a gap in the 'if and only if' of Stacks 0GJA for general torsion $F$, filled by this hypothesis, which every use of the lemma satisfies.)

source.place: Lemma 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof, last paragraph, remark (a); the hypothesis on F is added by the agent

proof.text: Part 2, assertions $(\mathcal C_4)$, $(\mathcal C_5)$ (Stacks remark (b) and the finiteness of $H^0(Z,i^{-1}F)$). Let $F'$ be constructible and either prime to $p$ (for $\mathcal C_4$ [def-weil-pbc-C4]) or $X$ be proper (for $\mathcal C_5$ [def-weil-pbc-C5]). For $(\mathcal C_4)$: if $F$ is $p$-primary (so $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$), $F'=0$ by step 3 and the conclusion is trivial; otherwise $F$ is prime to $p$ and constructible (hypothesis of the lemma), so $H^q(X,F)$ is finite for all $q$ by $\mathcal C_4(X,F)$. For $(\mathcal C_5)$: $F$ is constructible and $X$ proper, so $H^q(X,F)$ is finite by $\mathcal C_5(X,F)$. In both cases: $H^0(X,F')$ is a subgroup of the finite $H^0(X,F)$ by 7(ii); $H^1(X,F')$ is an extension of a subgroup of $H^1(X,F)$ by a quotient of the finite group $H^0(X,G)$ (step 4) by 7(ii), hence finite; and $H^q(X,F')\cong H^q(X,F)$ is finite for $q\ge2$ by 7(i).

source.place: Lemma 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof, remark (b) and the finiteness of the H^0 of Z

proof.text: Part 2, assertions $(\mathcal C_6)$, $(\mathcal C_7)$ (Stacks remark (c)). Let $k'/k$ be algebraically closed and either $F'$ prime to $p$ (for $\mathcal C_6$ [def-weil-pbc-C6]) or $X$ proper (for $\mathcal C_7$ [def-weil-pbc-C7]). In case $\mathcal C_6$ with $F$ $p$-primary, $F'=0$ (step 3) and the maps $\rho^q_{k'/k}(X,F')$ are isomorphisms between zero groups. Otherwise ($F$ prime to $p$, hence $G$ prime to $p$ by step 3, resp. $X$ proper) $\rho^q_{k'/k}(X,F)$ is an isomorphism for all $q$ by $\mathcal C_6(X,F)$ resp. $\mathcal C_7(X,F)$, and $\rho^q_{k'/k}(X,G)$ for all $q$ by step 6. In the morphism of long exact sequences of step 7 consider, for each $q\ge0$, the segment $H^{q-1}(F)\to H^{q-1}(G)\to H^q(F')\to H^q(F)\to H^q(G)$ over $X$ and its counterpart over $X_{k'}$ (with $H^{-1}=0$); the four outer vertical maps are isomorphisms, so the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] shows that $\rho^q_{k'/k}(X,F')$ is an isomorphism.

Part 2, assertion $(\mathcal C_8)$ (Stacks remark (d)). Let $a:U\hookrightarrow X$ be open and $b'\in H^2(U,a^{-1}F')$; let $b$ be its image in $H^2(U,a^{-1}F)$. By $\mathcal C_8(X,F)$ [def-weil-pbc-C8] there is $c\in H^2(X,F)$ with $a^*c=b$; by 7(i) $c$ is the image of some $c'\in H^2(X,F')$. By the commutativity of the ladder for $u=a$ (step 7), $a^*c'$ and $b'$ have the same image $b$ in $H^2(U,a^{-1}F)$, so $a^*c'=b'$ by 7(iii). Hence $a^*:H^2(X,F')\to H^2(U,a^{-1}F')$ is surjective. With the previous three steps, $\mathcal C(X,F')$ holds [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], which is part 2; parts 1 and 2 give the final equivalence, since a sheaf killed by a prime $r$ is $p$-primary if $r=p$ and prime to $p$ otherwise [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion].

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks 0GJA: closed complement Z finite set of k-points (step 2), sequence 0->j_!j^{-1}F->F->i_*i^{-1}F->0 of 095L (step 3), H^q(X,i_*E)=H^q(Z,E) via finite direct image exact + Leray identification and the zero-dimensional cohomology (step 4), its restriction to opens (step 5), C(X,i_*i^{-1}F) via the zero-dimensional nodes and the finite pushforward 0A5D (step 6), the long exact sequences and pullback ladders (step 7); direction C(j_!j^{-1}F)=>C(F) by the devissage 0A5C (step 8), the converse assertion by assertion from the cohomology sequence as Stacks does (steps 9-12). STATEMENT CORRECTED: the converse C(F)=>C(j_!j^{-1}F) is not derivable for (C3),(C4),(C6) when F mixes a p-primary and a prime-to-p part (e.g. F=j_!Z/l + i_*Z/p on an affine curve: C(X,F) says nothing about rho for j_!Z/l); part 2 now assumes F p-primary or prime to p, which holds in all three uses (sheaves killed by a prime). The 'again constructible' clause of the old statement is not needed by the proof and was dropped. Stacks 0GJA covers all eight assertions (1)-(8) = (C1)-(C8), each separately. No new nodes.

lean.statement: theorem IsCurve.dense_open_assertions {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (P : CurveCoefficientPair k) (hP : P.IsConstructible) (U : P.C.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set P.C)) : let E := (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} ℤ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).inv ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars (ULift.ringEquiv : ULift.{u + 1} ℤ ≃+* ℤ).toRingHom let F := (sheafCompose P.C.smallEtaleTopology E).obj P.F let F' := (Etale.openImmersionLowerShriek AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U.ι).obj ((Etale.upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U.ι).obj P.F) let G := (sheafCompose P.C.smallEtaleTopology E).obj F' (IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec G → IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec F) ∧ ((Scheme.IsTorsionSheafOfInvertibleOrder (Spec (.of k)) F ∨ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ CharP k p ∧ Scheme.IsPrimaryTorsionSheaf (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) F p) → IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec F → IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec G) ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, r.Prime → r • 𝟙 P.F = 0 → (IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec F ↔ IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec G))
